Review for Pet Clinic Gorai – Dr. Premal Darji

I am writing this with extreme pain after losing my beloved pet, Erika.

I was referred to Pet Clinic Gorai and trusted Dr. Premal Darji completely. That trust has turned into lifelong regret.

Erika had a tumor case, and instead of receiving clear surgical direction and decisive medical planning, her treatment kept getting prolonged with medications. During this period, her condition worsened, and she started experiencing severe bleeding episodes.

We repeatedly requested clarity about surgical intervention and long-term treatment planning. However, we never received firm guidance or urgency that such a critical case required.

At one stage, her platelet levels dropped significantly, and her bleeding became uncontrollable. Watching your pet lose blood helplessly while depending on professional guidance is something no pet parent should ever experience. Despite multiple visits and continuous follow-ups, her condition deteriorated rapidly.

We were left confused, emotionally shattered, and without clear answers.

If you are dealing with a serious or tumor-related condition, please:
– Ask for detailed blood reports and explanations
– Ask about platelet monitoring
– Seek immediate second opinions
– Do not delay critical decisions

Blind trust in medical situations can cost you everything. In our case, it cost us our family member.

The pain my family is going through cannot be described in words. Losing Erika has left a permanent void in our lives.

I hope no other pet parent has to go through this trauma.

featured_reviews.name: satyavir goswami
featured_reviews.review_text:
reply to Doctor Darji

We did not lose trust without reason. Trust was broken because there was no consistent line of treatment. Every visit we were told something different. If the prognosis was “clearly explained”, then why were we repeatedly given new approaches and delays?

You mentioned multiple opinions — but as pet parents, we depended on the primary treating doctor to guide us properly and urgently. Instead, there was confusion and no clear direction.

Regarding surgery — yes, amputation was discussed, but the risks and urgency were not explained in a way that reflected the seriousness of cancer progression. We were never clearly told that delay could drastically reduce survival chances. When referred, we were already emotionally and mentally exhausted due to lack of clear guidance.

If multiple vets were involved, that actually shows there was no single responsible direction. We kept running because we were not getting confident answers.

Please understand — this is not a “blame game.” This is about a life we lost. Erika was not just a case file for us. She was family.

We are not attacking professionals in general. We are questioning the inconsistency and delay in our specific case.

And as for reviews — people write from pain. Instead of questioning reviews, maybe reflect why pet parents feel unheard.

We hope no other pet parent goes through what we did.

featured_reviews.name: Jonita Quadras
featured_reviews.review_text:
We rescued our cat, Kiki, on January 29th 2025. A couple of weeks in, we suspected she might be pregnant and took her to Dr. Premal Darji. He strongly advised immediate spaying, assuring us it was completely safe and routine. Trusting his judgment, we went ahead with the surgery.

Soon after, Kiki began vomiting excessively — far more than what he described as “normal.” She stopped eating, peeing, or pooping. We visited his clinic daily post-op, but Dr. Darji had no clear answers. At one point, he even said he hadn’t “seen a case like this before,” but never recommended a specialist or second opinion.

Eventually, when we visited another vet, bloodwork revealed that Kiki’s creatinine was dangerously high (15) — a clear sign of acute kidney failure. We went back to Dr. Darji for an ultrasound, but again he insisted that “everything looked fine,” and failed to identify the actual issue. Even then, he didn’t show any urgency or transparency in managing the situation.

Desperate for help, we rushed her to Top Dog Clinic in Andheri, where they quickly diagnosed that urine was leaking into her abdomen, most likely due to trauma caused during the original spay surgery. They couldn’t keep her overnight, so we stabilized her at Blue 7 Vets in Borivali, and the next day, Top Dog performed a critical, life-saving surgery.

Kiki thankfully made it through, and while she still has one more surgery to go, she’s finally recovering. What’s most upsetting is that none of this had to happen. Dr. Darji never took accountability or gave us the information we needed to act sooner. His lack of proper communication and judgment not only endangered Kiki’s life but also left us emotionally drained and over ₹2 lakhs deep in treatment costs that could have been avoided.

This isn’t to spread hate, but to create awareness. If you feel unsure or uncomfortable with your vet’s advice, please don’t hesitate to seek a second opinion. Your pet’s life and your peace of mind are worth it.

featured_reviews.name: vikas nalawade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review about a stray cat named “Leopard” who eventually became our family member. Request you to please read it till end, as it may be helpful to any pet parent.
Leopard met with an accident and was missing for a week’s period. Later we found him & we noticed that he had a fracture at shoulder of right forelimb. Doctors told us that leg needs to be operated by inserting rod in his leg, so we got him operated by Dr. Sunetra. The surgery went well, but three days after surgery, Leopard's operated leg started swelling, we informed Dr. Sunetra but she told us it is the swelling due to surgery and it will subside downwards. But that swelling was due to infection and it lead to pus formation. Next day the swelling increased and in the evening pus started oozing out, seeing this we called up Dr. Sunetra & rushed to her with our Leopard. Dr. told us to keep flushing the wound twice a day with betadine. After 2-3 days of this treatment, the skin around the infected area went dead and we had a clear sight of his wound with operated area, where we could see his bone from two points because healing was not completed & the stitches were opened. We even asked Dr. Sunetra the doubt in our mind that this infection will not spread in his operated leg & internal body, to which she responded, it would not.
Eventually his external pain reduced but he had internal pain, which we failed to understand. He could not tolerate the pain and stopped eating and got fever exactly on 8th day from operation. We informed this situation of Leopard at every visit to Dr. Sunetra, but she recommended to force feed our Leopard. Later on our Leopard left with no energy to walk on his own and lift his neck, he even started heavy breathing. After informing this situation to Dr. Sunetra, she then advised us to put saline for his recovery but nowhere had she conveyed that Leopard’s health is deteriorating & he needs hospitalization. At this time, she was going out of town & was not available for 4-5 days.
Since, Dr. Sunetra was not available, we went to other Vet doctor who knew Leopard's medical history. This doctor told us to continue saline treatment twice a day for at least 4-5 days. Here the blood test was also done to examine the condition of our Leopard, where the report came with alarming & critical output depicting WBC increased & Platelets dropped to severe condition. Even this doctor also not recommended that our Leopard require hospitalization. This was the 11th day after operation.
The 12th day story (i.e. 1st July 23) of our Leopard was worst. The morning session of his saline was completed & even this second doctor went out of town for 3-4 days without recommending hospitalization. By evening, somewhere from 4:30pm, the heavy breathing became worse & we could not see his pain. We started calling Dr. Sunetra, but her phone was not reachable, so we text her on WhatsApp along with Leopard’s blood report. Since no response from doctor, with Leopard, we rushed to a Vet hospital, where he was admitted with a note by the doctors, like heavy breathing & drop in body temperature, which was very critical condition. He was kept in ICU incubator with oxygen supply to ease his breathe & improve his body temperature. The hospital doctors even told us that there are chances that the infection might have spread into blood. Unfortunately battling with pain & breathing problem our Leopard passed away on the same day around 11 pm.
There are certain questions for Dr. Sunetra;
# Why you haven't included any medicine for infection post-surgery?
# Why you did not advised us prior to start saline, when we informed you that Leopard lost his appetite?
# Why you did not look closely if the infection was spreading in the body? If you think it wasn't then why did he lost his appetite, had weakness, got fever, started heavy breathing?
# Why you took everything so lightly and casually in his case? Was it because it was a stray cat?

The doctor’s entire focus was on the operated area and the wound & the rest health parameters were ignored completely.
